title: Containment policy overshoot: region drain scoring overshoot, misroutes, and rollback playbook
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary:
On 2025-09-14 at ~03:10 UTC a control-plane change that adjusted region drain scoring (aimed at accelerating decommission of underutilized zones) caused an over-aggressive drain signal to propagate to multiple regional routers. The aggressive drain combined with a telemetry ingestion lag and a recent change to tier-weight bleed produced a wave of misrouting: requests were redirected from primary low-latency variants into fallbacks and higher-cost variants, causing a fallback surge and elevated tail latency for customers in affected regions.

Impact:
- ~12% throughput drop for the EU-west region for 52 minutes.
- 3.7x increase in requests served by fallback model variants in impacted tiers.
- Several production customers observed higher latency and token cost spikes; some triggered autoscale causing additional capacity churn.

Detection and mitigation timeline (high level):
- 03:10 UTC: automated drain-score rollout triggered by runtime-1.19 canary.
- 03:18 UTC: anomaly detectors (per-region routing divergence) fired; initial alert routed to SRE on-call.
- 03:20 UTC: Pager hits — multiple error-rate pages and latency escalation. Engineering triage convened.
- 03:22 UTC: Temporary traffic steering rule applied to pin critical routes to primary variants (manual override).
- 03:28 UTC: Canaries halted and drain-score change rolled back in control plane.
- 03:45 UTC: Normal routing pattern began to restore; full rollback completed by 03:55 UTC.

Root cause (detailed):
1) Drain scoring heuristic tweak: a recent tweak increased the weight on ephemeral metrics (instantaneous CPU pressure and short-window request drop) without adequate smoothing. This created high-variance scores for nodes under normal transient load.
2) Telemetry ingestion lag: the control plane uses a 30s sliding window of node metrics; a backend ingestion spike created a 40–70s delay in metrics becoming available, so the drain decision engine acted on partial/older data.
3) Tier-weight bleed change: a separate change reduced isolation between tiers (intended to improve utilization across bursty workloads). When combined with drained nodes, routing weights bled into fallback tiers more aggressively than expected.
4) Lack of a containment window: there was no enforced minimum retention for in-flight routing decisions (e.g., a short-lived drain should be rate-limited).

Contributing factors:
- Recent rollout of two independent runtime changes (drain-weight tuning and tier-bleed) were not coordinated.
- No automated rollback guard for control-plane decisions that impact >10% of regional traffic within 3 minutes.
- Insufficient end-to-end integration tests for composition of drain scoring + tier routing.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Manual rollback of drain scoring change via the rollout controller (03:28 UTC).
- Applied a manual pinning rule for high-priority customer routes to avoid fallback variants (03:22 UTC).
- Scoped a short-term traffic soft-cap to prevent autoscale thrash in affected clusters.

Longer-term remediation and actions (accepted):
- Add a containment window for drain signals: drain score transitions that exceed threshold must be stable for at least 90s before being actioned for traffic evacuation (action: ENG-100101, owner: Maya).
- Introduce a rollback guard in the control plane that automatically reverts configuration changes that cause >8% cross-variant reroute within a 5-minute sliding window (action: ENG-100102, owner: SRE).
- Revert and reintroduce tier-weight bleed change behind a feature flag and add end-to-end integration tests that simulate delayed telemetry (action: ENG-100103, owner: Runtime).
- Improve telemetry pipeline SLAs and add synthetic heartbeat metrics to reduce ingestion lag impact; add an alert when ingestion delay >20s (action: ENG-100104, owner: Observability).
- Create a routing shadow-run test harness to simulate canary drain scoring changes on historical traffic without affecting live routes (action: ENG-100105, owner: Routing QA).
- Update escalation runbooks to include a one-click emergency pin for critical customers and a documented rollback playbook (action: ENG-100106, owner: Oncall).

Post-incident notes and lessons learned:
- Independent small changes can interact in non-linear ways. We must require explicit coordination for any changes touching routing, tier allocation, or control-plane drain logic.
- Telemetry assumptions must be considered first-class safety constraints for control-plane actions.
- Implementing a conservative safety net (containment windows + automatic rollback) buys time for human assessment and reduces blast radius.

Artifacts and evidence (links):
- Grafana alert: https://grafana.redwood-internal/routing/divergence/alert-20250914
- Rollout change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/7f3c9a2
- Emergency pin PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/318
- Incident notes doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood-internal/display/INC/2025-09-14-region-drain

Current status:
- All code changes for the remediation (ENG-100101..ENG-100106) are in planning or early implementation; containment window and rollback guard tracked as P0 improvements.

resolution: Root cause identified as an over-aggressive drain scoring tweak combined with telemetry ingestion lag and tier-weight bleed. Immediate rollback restored routing; longer-term fixes include a containment window, automatic rollback guards, telemetry SLA improvements, and integration tests. Action items created and scheduled.
